title: Improved Lower Bounds for First-order Stochastic Non-convex Optimization under Markov Sampling
source_version: PMLR volume 267 published original; retrieved exact supplied PDF URL
summary: Theorem 3.1 is false at the explicit tau=1 hitting-time parameter; rare-state splitting does not preserve a fixed hitting bound. Algorithm 1 fails to maintain the weighted-gradient invariant used in the central convergence proof. A separate local TD-gradient reformulation is invalid.
limitations: All 19 pages read; full independent proofs of the remaining results were not performed.
No author code was available or executed; no experiments reproduced.
OpenReview separate attachments unavailable in acquired manifest; later revisions and errata not independently searched.
The algorithm invariant repair is verified algebraically, not as a repaired convergence theorem.

problems.title: Hitting-time class contradicts Theorem 3.1
problems.source_location: Definition 2.1 and equation (6), p.4; Theorem 3.1 and Remark 3.2, p.5; Appendix A.4, pp.13–15, equations (20)–(22)
problems.claim: For all positive parameters, including tau=1, Ns has a positive epsilon^-4 lower-bound term.
problems.assumptions: tau_hit maximizes expected positive hitting/return time over all pairs; stationary unbiasedness and variance upper bound; L-smooth F with gap <=Delta; zero-respecting algorithms.
problems.check: At tau=1 every hitting time must equal 1 almost surely. More than one state would require a row of the transition matrix to contain two entries equal to 1. Thus the sole state gives an exact gradient oracle. Gradient descent from zero is zero-respecting and achieves min gradient norm squared <=2LDelta/T. Fixing L=Delta=sigma=tau=1 contradicts the epsilon^-4 term as epsilon tends to zero. Splitting gives rare-state mass q*pi_v and positive return mean 1/(q*pi_v)>=1/q, violating fixed tau for small q.
problems.result: False theorem as stated; inadmissible rare-state construction at fixed hitting bound.
problems.counterevidence: Mixing time one would allow nontrivial iid sampling, but the displayed class uses hitting time. No repaired theorem under a different parameter is certified.
problems.impact: Principal lower-bound contribution directly affected; not a claim that every stochastic Markov lower bound is false.

correction.reason: Changing hitting time to mixing time requires revised classes and proof.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: The original defines tau_w using t>=1 and maximizes over v=w as well. Equation (6) really bounds this hitting/return time, not mixing time; Theorem 3.1 and Remark 3.2 explicitly include tau=1. Variance is an upper bound, so the singleton exact oracle remains allowed with sigma=1.
independent_check.decisive_check: Independently: an integer T>=1 with E[T]<=1 equals 1 almost surely. For every target w this would force P(v,w)=1, impossible for two distinct w. Thus tau=1 implies one state. Gradient descent with 1/L from 0 is zero-respecting and summing smooth descent gives min ||grad F||^2 <= 2LDelta/T. Selecting the lowest observed gradient or a uniform iterate meets the expected-norm requirement with O(epsilon^-2) samples, contradicting the positive epsilon^-4 coefficient at L=Delta=sigma=1. For the split construction on p.13, pi(v1)=q*pi(v); stationary reciprocal return time >=1/q violates fixed tau as q tends to zero.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: Changing to mixing time would change the written class. The lower-bound theorem as written is contradicted; no new lower bound or entire appendix certified. Core lower-bound dependency supports Major; proposed alternative is not a verified theorem repair.
independent_check.result: Supported as written; no scientific correction needed.

problems.title: Printed MaC-SAGE recurrence differs from proof invariant
problems.source_location: Algorithm 1 line 5 and subsequent weighted-gradient expression, p.6; Theorem B.5 decomposition, p.18
problems.claim: The displayed recurrence maintains G_t=sum_i y_t^i h_t^i.
problems.assumptions: Two iid states of equal stationary probability; f1=x^2/2+x, f2=x^2/2-x; L=sigma=1, Delta=1, tau=2; zero initialization; gamma0=1/8; positive-probability state path 1,2.
problems.check: G0=1, x1=-1/8, y1=(1/2,1/2), h1=(1,-9/8). Printed line 5 gives G1=7/16 whereas weighted sum=-1/16, a difference of 1/2. Unvisited-state weight decay is missing. Scaling the old sum and removed term by t/(t+1) restores the invariant by induction.
problems.result: Core convergence derivation uses an invariant not obeyed by the printed algorithm.
problems.counterevidence: The intended weighted-gradient algorithm might admit a bound. This finite counterexample does not prove divergence or refute every possible rate analysis of the printed recursion.
problems.impact: Direct dependency of Theorem 4.4/B.5 on the false decomposition supports Major.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Algorithm 1 line 5 does not scale G_(t-1) by t/(t+1), whereas line 4 scales every old frequency. Theorem B.5 p.18 replaces G by the frequency-weighted stale gradients. Quadratic components have L=1 globally, noise magnitude 1, gap zero <=1, and the iid uniform chain has positive return/hitting mean 2.
independent_check.decisive_check: Fresh manual substitution on path (1,2): at t=0 G=1, x1=-1/8; at t=1 the old state-2 table is zero, so printed G1=1+(1/2)(-9/8)=7/16. The claimed sum is (1/2)*1+(1/2)*(-9/8)=-1/16. The difference 1/2 persists for any first stepsize. Multiplying the old sum and removed visited contribution by t/(t+1) updates exactly every unvisited weight and hence restores the invariant by induction.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: An intended corrected SAG recurrence can differ from the printed code; the report explicitly limits the repair to the invariant and does not claim divergence or a repaired rate. The false identity is used in the central convergence derivation, so Major remains supported.

problems.title: TD vector field lacks the claimed scalar potential
problems.source_location: Section 2.1, p.3, line-integral definition and equation (3)
problems.claim: The line integral f has gradient equal to the per-sample TD vector field g.
problems.assumptions: Two states with features e1,e2, zero reward, gamma=1/2, theta*=0; iid chain has positive probability of the transition e1 to e2; theta0=0.
problems.check: g=(x-y/2,0), whereas f=x^2/2-xy/4 has gradient (x-y/4,-x/4). At (0,1), values are (-1/2,0) and (-1/4,0). The nonsymmetric Jacobian prevents a scalar potential.
problems.counterevidence: Conservative fields or special expected TD fields can have potentials; neither establishes the claimed per-sample identity.
problems.impact: Motivating application affected; no dependence of the abstract lower-bound proofs demonstrated.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Source p.3 explicitly claims the radial line integral differentiates to the per-transition g. Zero reward and theta*=0 satisfy exact linear value representation with two independent basis features; gamma=1/2 is admissible.
independent_check.decisive_check: Independently expanded the TD field for transition e1 to e2: g=(x-y/2,0). Along the radius u(x,y), the integrand is u*(x^2-xy/2), giving f=x^2/2-xy/4. Differentiation gives (x-y/4,-x/4), unequal at (0,1). Cross derivatives of g are -1/2 and 0, ruling out another differentiable scalar potential on this domain.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: A conservative expected field or special features do not prove this asserted per-sample identity. The dependency is the motivating TD reformulation, with no demonstrated lower-bound dependency, so Minor is appropriate.
